memory_candidates.content: When re-deriving a 'same-session vs. cross-session' wall-clock delta classification from git history for a recurring-gate cost study, do not use an arbitrary time-magnitude threshold as a same-session proxy -- match the commit body's `Session:` trailer exactly between the two paired commits instead. In this corpus the magnitude threshold happened to agree with the session-trailer match, but only coincidentally; the trailer is the actual ground truth and is cheap to extract with `git log --format='%x01%H%x02%ad%x02%s%x02%b%x03'` plus a regex on the body.

deploy-headless.sh's inline fast-gate pass can fail gate10 (validate-state.sh --deep specs/state.json) on its internal 60s timeout purely from concurrent sibling write load on a shared specs/state.json during a multi-task /orchestrate batch, even though a direct, untimed re-run of the same command passes cleanly in ~68s. Before treating a gate10 timeout as a content regression, re-run the underlying check directly outside the inline timeout to distinguish a load-induced timing artifact from a real failure.
